raw_response:
My land is only 3.5 mu, so I must think carefully. I grow spring maize like my neighbors. Last year I got about 550 kg per mu, which was acceptable. I will do similar this year.

For seeds, I buy hybrid from the village dealer — everyone uses Zhengdan or similar. Old seeds give low yield, no one plants them anymore. About 2 kg seed for my 3.5 mu.

For fertilizer, before planting I put compound fertilizer (15-15-15), about 40 kg per mu as base. Then at big trumpet stage I topdress urea, maybe 20 kg per mu. So nitrogen total comes to around 15 kg per mu, phosphorus and potassium each around 6 kg per mu. I do not want to save money here — if maize is hungry, the ears will be small and I lose much more than I save. Fertilizer is expensive but skipping is worse.

I have well water, so I irrigate when the weather is dry. Usually I water after sowing to help seeds come up, then once at jointing, once at tasseling if no rain. Three times is enough.

Pests — I spray once for armyworm when I see them, sometimes twice if borer is bad. I buy cheap pesticide at village shop.

I use the small tractor from the village service for rotary tillage before sowing. Plough is too expensive to hire.
